findings.reason: the mechanism needs either a bounded trigger for the prefix check (only where a rewrite can arise) or a paragraph saying the prefix is re-read each tick with a measure covering those bytes; as written the section both promises offset-only reads and specifies a per-tick full-prefix read, and its done-when cannot see the difference.
findings.text: "whose first 4 KiB no longer match the digest stored beside its offset" makes every tick re-read 4 KiB of every live stream from GPFS before the offset read; at even 30 live streams and a 2 s tick that is roughly 3.6 MB/min, 18% of §3's whole 20 MB/min crew-monitor budget, spent re-reading bytes the design says it reads once, and paragraph 1's "a stream is read only past its stored offset" is false as soon as the digest clause is read with it

findings.reason: one line naming what the replacement asserts (the incremental store's pointer paths compared to the fixture's three) makes the third repair reviewable, and without it a gate passes on two of three carried items.
findings.text: of the §5 review items §6 adopts, the dead wrappers are measured (`git grep` returns nothing) and the connection leak is measured (fd count equal), but "replaces the assertion in `tests/test_the_station_store_is_node_local.py` that compares two outputs of the store with one against the fixture's three pointer paths" carries no measure, so the node can close §6 with the equivalence assertion still in place
